{
  "need": "Status",
  "secondary": { "name": "Competence" },
  "read": "This student may have genuinely leveled up, and your doubt, if they sense it, lands as a public verdict that they are not capable of real work. Even if something is off, what is most at stake is their sense of being seen as someone who can produce something worthy of respect. The competence angle shows up in whichever direction this goes: if it was theirs, they need to know you believe it; if it was not, they need to know they can actually get there.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Calling them out or leading with suspicion, which signals you assume the worst and shames them before you know anything, poisoning the relationship even if you turn out to be right." },
  "mentorMove": "Treat the work as an opportunity to go deeper, not a crime scene to investigate. Have a genuine conversation about the thinking behind it, which tells you what you need to know while conferring the respect that says you take their growth seriously either way.",
  "holdFirm": ["The standard is that the work has to be theirs, produced with their own thinking, and that does not move.", "They need to be able to talk through the ideas, the choices they made, and what was hard, because that is what ownership looks like."],
  "stayFlexible": ["How you have that conversation can feel like a celebration of growth rather than an interrogation.", "You can let them lead: ask them to walk you through it, share what they are proud of, explain a decision, which is natural for strong work and revealing without being adversarial."],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 2, "label": "Questions" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, I read your work last night and I want to talk about it with you. I am not pulling you aside because something is wrong. I just do not want to just put a grade on this and move on." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "Walk me through it a little. What were you trying to do here, and where did you find yourself having to think the hardest? I am genuinely asking, not quizzing you." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Okay, here is where I want to land. If this thinking is yours, I want to make sure you know how to get back to it and keep building on it, because that is actually the skill. What support would help you do that next time?" },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I hold everyone to the standard that the work has to come from your own thinking, and I am holding you to it too because I think you are actually capable of the real thing. What I saw here, if you can own it and build on it, is the kind of work that matters. I want that to be yours." }
  ],
  "longGame": "Whatever you discover, the goal is that this student leaves the conversation feeling like someone who is capable of growth, not someone who is suspected of cheating or protected from accountability. If the work was genuinely theirs, your curiosity confirms that you take them seriously as a thinker. If it was not, you have opened a door where they can tell the truth without being humiliated, which is the only condition under which real learning can follow."
}
situation: A student handed in work far better than anything they have produced before, and I genuinely cannot tell if it is a breakthrough or if someone else did it.
